title: Speaking
subtitle: whisper, mutter, object to, angrily
summary: Report what people say and how they say it - whisper, mumble, shriek - and use the verbs and adverbs that show the speaker's mood and intention.

lesson.heading: Reporting verbs: how loud, and what mood
lesson.note: People also whisper in places where it would be impolite to speak loudly. Stuttering and stammering may also be the result of a speech impediment.

lesson.heading: Using the reporting verbs
lesson.text: These verbs can introduce direct speech or a reported clause. In writing they save you a whole sentence of explanation.

examples.text: 'I'm sick of this. I'm going home,' he **muttered**.
She **whispered** that she was not happy with the way the meeting was going.

lesson.heading: Verbs that show feelings and intentions
lesson.note: Most of these verbs can also take a that clause: She **boasted that** she had scored 20 goals in one season. He **threatened (that)** he would call the police.

lesson.heading: Verb plus adverb
lesson.text: To show how someone feels, pair a speaking verb with an adverb. This is very common in written style.

examples.text: 'I feel much better today, thank you,' Andrew **said happily**.
'I'm very worried. She said she would phone us,' Rory **said anxiously**.
'We may be lucky and the rain might stop,' Anna **said hopefully**.

lesson.text: Reluctantly is the adverb for doing something you do not really want to do: 'All right, I'll come,' he said reluctantly.

exercises.prompt: 'Don't look now, but Matt has just arrived,' she ___ in my ear.
exercises.explanation: You whisper a secret very softly.

exercises.prompt: 'Joey! Come here at once!!' his mother ___.
exercises.explanation: Shout is loud and usually angry or excited.
Stutter and stammer suggest nervousness or excitement.

exercises.prompt: 'I'm sick of this meeting. I'm going home,' he ___.
'Oh, that's so, so funny!' she ___ with laughter.
exercises.explanation: A shriek is loud and shrill, from fright or amusement.
A scream is loud and usually without words.

exercises.prompt: 'Stop ___! I can't hear what you're saying,' she said.
exercises.explanation: Mumbling is soft and unclear, often from nervousness.

exercises.prompt: 'I think we should leave now. It's late,' he ___ quietly.
exercises.explanation: Murmur is soft; it suits a quiet, private remark.

exercises.prompt: Match the sentence beginnings with their endings.

pairs.right: that he could read people's minds.
that he needed a doctor immediately.
about the noise coming from above.
not to leave, but I had to.
on using recycled paper for everything.

exercises.prompt: Match each remark with the adverb that best describes how it was said.

pairs.left: I feel much better today, thank you.
Oh wow! I've just won a prize in a competition!
I will never forgive them for what they did.
This is our last day together. I'll miss you.
Oh, come on! Do hurry up! Let's go! Now!
We may be lucky and the rain might stop.

exercises.prompt: Don't ___ about your talents to your friends. They'll stop liking you.
exercises.explanation: You boast to someone about something when you are proud of yourself.

exercises.prompt: I ___ to having to sit on the floor. I paid for a seat.
exercises.explanation: Object to + -ing shows you are unhappy with a situation.

exercises.prompt: Stop ___ about your job all the time.
exercises.explanation: Grumble about something means complain about it repeatedly.
Beg someone to do something shows desperation.

exercises.prompt: He talked about refusing to pay and calling the police. Which is the correct rewrite?
options: He threatened to refuse to pay and to call the police.
He threatened refusing to pay and calling the police.
He threatened on refusing to pay.
He threatened about refusing to pay.
exercises.explanation: Threaten is followed by to + infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Let's be friends. I don't want to argue ___ you.
exercises.explanation: You argue with someone about something.

exercises.prompt: Which adverb means that someone does not want to do something?
Do these adverbs describe positive or negative feelings?

exercises.answer: She whispered that she was not happy with the way the meeting was going.
exercises.explanation: Whisper can introduce a that clause as well as direct speech.
